title: The six-operations package
statement:
Fix the coefficient stages of [sk-def-sf-setting] and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. All squares and products below are
in this category. At finite coefficients use ordinary small étale categories
and their étale-origin pro-étale realizations; at integral coefficients use
derived-complete pro-étale objects and completed pullback and tensor, at
$E$ their raw rationalization, and at $\Qlb$ common finite coefficient
stages. The operations of [sk-def-sf-operations] have precisely these
coefficient domains. The exceptional operation $Rf^!$ is the constructible
one, not an unconditional right adjoint on the whole pro-étale derived
category. The following assertions include descent to the small categories
with the domains of [thm-sf-ctf-stability].

1. **(1)** *Adjunctions.* At finite coefficients the module inverse image $Lf^*$ is exact, hence preserves
bounded-below objects, and its restriction
$Lf^*:D^+(Y,\Lambda)\to D^+(X,\Lambda)$ is left adjoint to
$Rf_*:D^+(X,\Lambda)\to D^+(Y,\Lambda)$:
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(X,\Lambda)}(Lf^*K,L)\cong \operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(Y,\Lambda)}(K,Rf_*L)$, naturally in
$K\in D^+(Y,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^+(X,\Lambda)$ (both functors typed between
the same pair of categories); at the other coefficient stages the ordinary adjunction restricts to the specified bounded constructible categories. The constructible exceptional adjoint
$Rf^!:\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sf-operations] (vi) is
right adjoint to $Rf_!:\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$,
unconditionally, with units and counits compatible with composition,
refinements and exchanges ([thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions],
[thm-sf-ctf-stability], [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]); and, at a finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$, whenever $f$ carries the ambient datum of
[sk-def-sf-admissible] (1), the ambient functor
$Rf_!:D(X,A)\to D(Y,A)$ is left adjoint to the ambient functor
$Rf^{\times}:D(Y,A)\to D(X,A)$ of [sk-def-sf-operations] (v).
When this same ambient adjoint also satisfies the preservation clauses (2)–(3)
of [sk-def-sf-admissible], its restriction to $\Dctf$ agrees with $Rf^!$.
The ambient datum alone does not include these preservation clauses.
1. **(2)** *Base change.* For every Cartesian square the exchange
transformation $\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!\to Rf'_!Lg'^*$ of
[sk-def-sf-exchanges] is a natural isomorphism with the respective typings of
[thm-cbc-finite-torsion], [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale],
[thm-cbc-complete-proetale], [thm-cbc-finite-extension] and [thm-cbc-qbar] — at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ on $D^+$ of the small étale site
and on the étale-origin complexes of the pro-étale site; at
$\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$ only on $\Dbc$ of the adic pro-étale categories, as
the completed exchange, and never on the discrete non-torsion coefficients of
the small étale site, exactly as for $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ below; it is the
identity for the identity square,
compatible with pasting of squares, independent of the compactification
(compatible with the refinement comparisons of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed])
and compatible with the composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and its completed and scalar transports,
the last two on the finite-stage étale-origin complexes of [sk-def-sf-operations] (iv) and on the stated completed and transported domains
([thm-cbc-finite-torsion]).
The exchange transformation $\operatorname{Ex}_*:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lg'^*$ is a
natural isomorphism for proper $f$ ([sk-thm-properbasechange]) and for
smooth $g$ ([sk-thm-smooth-base-change]), *with the following typing
only*: (a) at a finite stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, as functors
$D^+(X,\Lambda)\to D^+(Y',\Lambda)$ on the small étale site and on the
étale-origin complexes of the pro-étale site (for smooth $g$ on the bounded
constructible ones); (b) at the stages
$\mathcal O_E$, $E$, $\Qlb$, only on $\Dbc$ of the pro-étale (adic)
categories — derived-complete $\mathcal O_E$-complexes whose reductions are
of étale origin, their rationalizations and the $\Qlb$-colimit, with
$\operatorname{Ex}_*$ the completed exchange — where the proper case is [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete],
[thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension], [thm-weil-pbc-qbar]. In this finite-type setting the finite-level étale-origin and uniform
constructible-interval hypotheses of [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change], and
the square-constructible lattice and common-stage hypotheses of
[sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] and
[sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch], hold for every
object in the specified bounded constructible category: integral finite
reductions have a common Tor interval, the finite direct-image dimension
bounds and exact pullbacks bound all four corner expressions, and raw
rationalization supplies an integral representative. Thus the smooth
exchange also lands in the bounded constructible category without an
additional hypothesis on its input.
The maps are the completed finite-tower exchange and its scalar transports. No
assertion is made for the discrete non-torsion coefficients $\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$
on the small étale site, where $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ is not an isomorphism in
general.
1. **(3)** *Projection formula.* $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an
isomorphism for $K\in\Dbc(X,A_{E,n})$ and $L\in\Dctf(Y,A_{E,n})$
at finite coefficients, and for $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and
$L\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)=\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ at the integral and field stages,
with the completed tensor at the integral stage. It is an isomorphism in
the respective ambient category, natural and
coherent, including compatible with base change through the
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of clause (2) (the base-change clause of
[prop-sf-pf-coherence])
([sk-thm-sf-pf-finite], [prop-sf-pf-reduction],
[thm-sf-pf-adic], [thm-sf-pf-field], [sk-thm-sf-pf-proetale],
[prop-sf-pf-coherence]).
1. **(4)** *Compactifications and proper coincidence.*
$Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ (at finite level on étale-origin inputs, and at higher levels with the completed and transported interpretation) is independent of the compactification with the composition
law $R(gf)_!\cong Rg_!Rf_!$, and $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$
([prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], [thm-sf-comp-composition],
[cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]).
1. **(5)** *Orientation.* For smooth $f$ of pure relative dimension $d$
the purity map $\gamma_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\to Rf^!K$ (the orientation of
[sk-def-sf-orientation]) is a natural isomorphism of functors
$\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$; in particular
$\omega_f\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ ([thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], with
[sk-thm-purity-transport] for the remaining coefficient stages). It is
compatible with composition of smooth morphisms (twist additivity, through
the mate isomorphism $R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]) and with
base change — along arbitrary $g$ at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, along étale $g$ at
the other stages — where the smooth pullback exchange
$Lg'^*Rf^!\to Rf'^!Lg^*$ is [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange].
At finite coefficients its counit description is the transpose under
$Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$ of
$Rf'_!Lg'^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}}Lg^*Rf_!Rf^!K
\xrightarrow{Lg^*\varepsilon_f}Lg^*K$;
this is distinct from the right-adjoint conjugate
$Rg'_*Rf'^!\to Rf^!Rg_*$. Under
$\gamma_f,\gamma_{f'}$ it becomes the canonical isomorphism
$Lg'^*Lf^*\cong Lf'^*Lg^*$, i.e. the trace (the exceptional counit read
through $\gamma$) is compatible with $\operatorname{Ex}_!$. At
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ it is compatible with the exceptional Künneth map: for
smooth $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ of pure relative dimensions $d_i$ and
$L_i\in\Dctf(Y_i,\Lambda)$, the map $\alpha$ of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] (ii)
corresponds under $\gamma_{f_1}\boxtimes\gamma_{f_2}$ and
$\gamma_{f_1\times f_2}$ to the canonical pullback–tensor isomorphism
$Lf_1^*L_1(d_1)[2d_1]\boxtimes Lf_2^*L_2(d_2)[2d_2]\cong
L(f_1\times f_2)^*(L_1\boxtimes L_2)(d_1+d_2)[2d_1+2d_2]$ (the smooth comparison is obtained by transposing the product of the normalized smooth traces; no general Künneth–Verdier assertion is needed).
1. **(6)** *Duality.* With $\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ formed from the
constructible exceptional adjoint of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi) (no
admissibility datum is assumed; [thm-sf-biduality-class] is
unconditional),
$\mathbb D_X:\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$,
$\mathbb D_X=\RHom_X(-,\omega_X)$ with $\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$, is a
contravariant exact anti-equivalence,
and the biduality morphism $\delta_K:K\to\mathbb D_X\mathbb D_XK$ (the
tensor–Hom transpose of the evaluation
$K\otimes^L_\Lambda\mathbb D_XK\to\omega_X$) is a natural isomorphism
$\delta:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb D_X\mathbb D_X$
([thm-sf-biduality-class]). For every separated finite-type $f$,
the Verdier exchange map
$\varepsilon_{f,M}:\mathbb D_Y(Rf_!M)\to Rf_*\mathbb D_X(M)$ of
[sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange] — the tensor–Hom isomorphism of
[sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] at $N=\omega_Y$ followed by
$Rf_*\RHom_X(M,-)$ of the mate isomorphism $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$ —
is a natural isomorphism in the respective ambient category for $M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$; it
is compatible with composition: for $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$,
$\varepsilon_{gf,M}$ agrees, through $\mathbb D_Z(\alpha_{g,f})$ and
$R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*Rf_*$, with
$Rg_*(\varepsilon_{f,M})\circ\varepsilon_{g,Rf_!M}$ (associativity of
$\operatorname{PF}$, [prop-sf-pf-coherence], and the mate calculus
[lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]). No compatibility of
$\varepsilon$ with base change along an arbitrary $g$ is asserted
($\mathbb D$ does not commute with $Lg^*$ in general).
Unconditionally, for $X$ smooth of pure dimension $d$ and perfect $K$, the
orientation-induced
isomorphism $\theta_K:\mathbb D_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$ of
[sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect] is natural in $K$
([sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect]); for $X$ satisfying the smooth, geometrically connected and proper-or-finite-field-descent hypotheses of [sk-thm-sf-global-duality], the
global duality map $\RG_c(X,K)^\vee\to\RG(X,\mathbb D_XK)$ of
[sk-thm-sf-global-duality] is an isomorphism in the point category; and for site-perfect $K$ under these same hypotheses the
derived Poincaré pairing is perfect and is the duality isomorphism
([sk-thm-sf-identification]).
1. **(7)** *Relative product.*
Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $f:X\to B$ and
$g:Y\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms, and let
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$.
Writing $p:X\times_BY\to X$ and $q:X\times_BY\to Y$ for the projections,
put $K\boxtimes L=Lp^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lq^*L$ and
$f\times_Bg=gq=fp$. The relative Künneth map
$\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{K,L}:R(f\times_Bg)_!(K\boxtimes L)\to
Rf_!K\otimes^LRg_!L$ of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] (the composite of the
composition law, the inverse projection transformations for $q$ and $g$ and
the inverse of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$) is a natural isomorphism in
the respective ambient category over $B$, compatible with symmetry, triple products, base change
$B'\to B$ and the projection formula as stated there (the symmetry and
base-change compatibilities rest on the base-change clause of
[prop-sf-pf-coherence], i.e. on clause (3)), with its
compact-support form on closed subschemes ([sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative]).
1. **(8)** *Stability.* The operations descend to the constructible and
finite-Tor subcategories exactly as typed in [thm-sf-ctf-stability], with the following Tor-amplitude intervals at finite coefficients and uniformly on integral finite reductions (field-stage bounds are read on integral representatives):
$[a,b+2d]$ for $Rf_*$ when $\dim X\le d$, $[a+c,b+d']$ for $\otimes^L$, $[c-b-2d,d'-a+2d]$
for $\RHom$ of objects with amplitudes $[a,b],[c,d']$ on a scheme of
dimension $\le d$ ($[c-b,d'-a]$ for a site-perfect first argument), and
for $Rf^!$ the shifts supplied by smooth purity, [prop-exc-closed-tor] and [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum]: $-2d$ for
$f$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, $[a,b]\mapsto[a,b+2d+1]$ for a
closed immersion into a target of dimension $\le d$ (a target-dimension
bound; no codimension-only bound is asserted for arbitrary closed
immersions), and $[a,b]\mapsto[a-2D,b+2\dim Y+1]$ in the general case, $D$
the maximum number of relative affine-space coordinates in a chosen finite
family of closed affine-chart presentations $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$
[cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum]. This means $D=\max_U d_U$, not an
unspecified absolute embedding dimension. Empty schemes have the zero category;
no dimension or maximum of an empty chart family is used.

source.place: node sk-thm-sf-package, order 2514

proof.text: Fix the coefficient and operation constructions of [sk-def-sf-setting] and [sk-def-sf-operations]. Use precisely their constant finite coefficients, completed integral coefficients, raw rationalizations and common finite stages. The global datum has $\ell\ne p$, so each finite coefficient ring is annihilated by an integer invertible on every corner. Squares are within the finite-type category: their corners are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied over the field and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; base change preserves separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. These facts verify the geometric and coefficient hypotheses in the steps below. The absolute structural exceptional functor is typed because each scheme here is separated over $k$. Finite type includes quasi-compactness; separated implies quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal. Thus the application of the Noetherian finite-type theorem has an explicit Noetherian base. The target is also quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], so [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies each required compactification. Its proper part is finite type, and its ambient scheme is finite type over $k$: on finite affine covers, generators for the proper-part algebras together with generators for the base algebras generate the composite algebras. Therefore [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] also supplies a finite dimension bound for the chosen compactification in the bounded-class adjoint theorem.

source.place: Opening setting; common hypotheses of clauses (1)–(8)

proof.text: At finite coefficients the inverse image on module sheaves is exact and left adjoint to module direct image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and on the pro-étale site exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Its derived functor is termwise inverse image, so $H^i(Lf^*K)=f^*H^i(K)$ and a lower bound is preserved. Apply the derived-adjunction theorem [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] to this adjunction and the derived functors of [sk-def-sf-operations]. This gives the stated natural Hom bijections on $D^+$; at finite pro-étale level restrict the same exact derived pullback and right-derived direct image. At the other coefficient stages use [fix-prop-adjunctions](1), which is an adjunction on $D^b_c$, not on unspecified non-torsion étale $D^+$ categories.

source.place: Clause (1): ordinary adjunction, exactness and domains

proof.text: For the constructible exceptional adjunction, the finite ordinary étale adjoint and its bounded-below comparison-class adjunction are [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2)–(3). Every bounded constructible finite pro-étale input has étale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. For the specified transported exceptional functor, [thm-sf-ctf-stability](iv),(v) gives preservation of the finite-Tor constructible categories by both $Rf_!$ and $Rf^!$. Since these subcategories are full, the same natural Hom bijections restrict to them, giving the finite-stage adjunction. The integral construction, finite reductions and compatibility of units and counits are stated in [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], rationally in [lem-coef-rational-operations], and at a common algebraically closed stage in [thm-coef-qbar-verdier]. Thus $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ is unconditional on the displayed small categories. This argument does not invoke an unrestricted ambient adjoint or identify it with a localizing-subcategory adjoint.

source.place: Clause (1): constructible exceptional adjunction at each coefficient stage

proof.text: The optional ambient datum [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] includes its right adjoint, so the ambient adjunction asserted conditionally in (1) is part of that datum. A restriction of this functor to $\Dctf$ can be made only if its preservation clauses (2)–(3) in [sk-def-sf-admissible] also hold. Under those clauses both restricted functors are right adjoints of the same restricted $Rf_!$; [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identifies them by the unique counit-compatible isomorphism. No subsequent step uses this optional assertion.

source.place: Clause (1): optional ambient assertion and its conditional restriction

proof.text: At finite coefficients [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] identifies the candidates $R\bar f_*j_!$ on witnessed inputs; its identity, transitivity and common-refinement independence give compactification independence. [thm-sf-comp-composition] supplies the canonical composition comparison with its identity and associativity equations. For proper $f$, choose $j=\mathrm{id}$ and $p=f$; [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] identifies this candidate with $Rf_*$ and its exchange with proper base change. At the integral, rational and common-stage coefficients, [prop-functor-package](2),(3) states the compactification comparisons with refinement independence and cocycle condition, the composition isomorphism $R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$ with its identity and associativity equations, and $Rf_!\simeq Rf_*$ for proper $f$; [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4) records that the compact-support exchanges are compatible with these completed and scalar-transported composition identifications on precisely their coefficient domains. They therefore give (4) at the remaining stages; no finite-origin comparison is extended to arbitrary unbounded pro-étale inputs.

source.place: Clause (4): compactifications, composition, proper coincidence

proof.text: For the compact-support part of (2), apply [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] to $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_{E,n})$. Its specified exchange is invertible, independent of the compactification and satisfies identity and both pasting equations. [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] gives exactly the transported exchange for a witnessed finite pro-étale input, independently of the witness. These are statements about the exchange map itself, not merely existence of an isomorphism between its endpoints.

source.place: Clause (2): finite compact-support base change

proof.text: For an integral input use its compatible finite-reduction witnesses, which are part of the specified coefficient domain. [thm-cbc-complete-proetale] identifies the completed exchange as proper completed exchange followed by the completed open comparison, equivalently the ordered derived-limit comparison of the finite maps. It proves that composite invertible, with identity, pasting and refinement equations. [thm-cbc-finite-extension] applies raw rationalization to this same map, proves independence of the integral lattice and its naturality in rational morphisms. [thm-cbc-qbar] represents the exchange after a common finite overfield and proves independence of the representative. Finally [fix-lem-exchanges](4) supplies compatibility with composition and refinement on these domains. This proves the higher-stage compact-support assertions of (2).

source.place: Clause (2): completed and scalar compact-support exchange, including coherence

proof.text: For proper $f$, [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] gives the finite étale exchange for every bounded-below torsion complex. [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] identifies the forgotten module exchange with that abelian exchange and reflects invertibility, so this is the $A_{E,n}$-linear map in (2). [thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale] gives its exact finite pro-étale form on witnessed inputs. For higher stages [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete], [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension] and [thm-weil-pbc-qbar] give respectively the completed exchange, its raw rationalization and common-stage descent. The base-changed morphism is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The dimension and Noetherian hypotheses were checked in step 1; [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] supplies the required finite uniform fiber-dimension bound, because the target is quasi-compact. Its scheme-theoretic fibre bound is also a geometric fibre bound: for a geometric point over $y$, the fibre is the base change of the finite-type $\kappa(y)$-scheme $X_y$ to its geometric residue field, and [lem-kun-dimension-extension] preserves its dimension under this field extension.

source.place: Clause (2): ordinary proper exchange at finite, completed and scalar stages

proof.text: For smooth $g$ relabel the square in [sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change] so its smooth horizontal arrow is $g$ and its quasi-compact quasi-separated vertical direct-image arrow is $f$. The separated finite-type condition gives qcqs. Its input is torsion of invertible orders because the finite coefficient ring is $\ell$-primary and $\ell$ is invertible. [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] identifies the module map with that exchange. [sbc-thm-finite-proetale-smooth-base-change] gives the finite pro-étale exchange for bounded constructible witnessed inputs. For integral $K$, the compatible étale-origin witnesses are part of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] makes each reduction a bounded constructible étale-origin object. Choose a cohomology interval $[a,b]$ for $K_1$; [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives that same finite Tor interval for every $K_n$. Choose nonnegative dimension bounds $d_X,d_{X'}$ (zero at an empty corner). By [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i),(iii), all finite direct images and pullbacks in the square are constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Specifically $Rf_{n,*}K_n$ has interval $[a,b+2d_X]$, and [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible] preserves its cohomology interval under $Lg_n^*$. The other input $Lg_n'^*K_n$ has cohomology interval $[a,b]$ and finite Tor interval $[a,b]$: exact inverse image commutes with tensor and stalks, so its stalk Tor tests are the input stalk tests. Applying (iii) to $f'$ gives interval $[a,b+2d_{X'}]$ for $Rf'_{n,*}Lg_n'^*K_n$. Hence the common cohomology interval $[a,b+2\max(d_X,d_{X'})]$ works for all four objects and all $n$. These are precisely the interval hypotheses of [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] and the square-constructible predicate of [sbc-def-admissible-lattices], not an assumed identification of reductions with pushforwards. The integral theorem therefore gives the completed exchange in $D^b_c$. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], a raw rational object has an integral representative (the same object), so the preceding argument gives a square-constructibly admissible lattice for every such object. Apply [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change]. For [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], each object and morphism has a common finite field stage. [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] preserves these bounded constructible categories and identifies the scalar-extended exchange; the argument just given applies to every integral representative at every larger stage. Thus all hypotheses of [sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch] hold. Its ambient isomorphism has constructible endpoints because the two endpoints are represented by the already constructible $E$-stage endpoints. The maps are the completed mate and its scalar extensions, as identified by [fix-lem-exchanges](3). The unchanged finite Tor interval under pullback is also stated directly by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], applied to $g_n$ and $g_n^\prime$; both are separated finite type in the stated square category.

source.place: Clause (2): smooth exchange and exact higher-coefficient scope

proof.text: For (3), $K\in D^b_c(X,A_{E,n})$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$ are exactly the hypotheses of [sk-thm-sf-pf-finite], so its specified projection transformation is an isomorphism. [fix-prop-projection-formula] gives the same map on the completed integral, rational and common-stage categories, including naturality, finite reduction on finite-Tor inputs, compactification comparisons and proper coincidence. [sk-thm-sf-pf-proetale] supplies its pro-étale identification on finite-Tor witnessed pairs. At the integral and field stages $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii), so there is no missing finite-Tor hypothesis. No proper projection theorem with uncompleted condensed coefficients is substituted for this completed compact-support formula.

source.place: Clause (3): specified projection map and coefficient domains

proof.text: For (6), [thm-sf-biduality-class] states directly that $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,Ra_X^!\Lambda)$ is an exact anti-equivalence on $D^b_{ctf}$ at finite coefficients and on the specified $D^b_c$ at the other stages, with the evaluation-defined natural biduality map. This also supplies the dualizing objects needed below. In its current statement the numerical bound is expressed using an integer $d_X\ge0$ with $\dim X\le d_X$: an input Tor interval $[a,b]$, $a\le b$, gives $[-b-2d_X,-a]$, and the dualizing object has interval $[-2d_X,0]$, uniformly on finite reductions at integral coefficients. Step 1 supplies a finite dimension bound; take $d_X=\dim X$ for nonempty $X$ and $d_X=0$ for empty $X$. In the empty case all objects and their duals are zero, so these are valid integer intervals. Field duals are computed from integral representatives at a common finite coefficient field before localization. All functors, adjunctions, base-change isomorphisms, projection maps, composition maps and biduality used in (A1)–(A6) of [def-sf-datum] have now been supplied on their stated domains; the coefficient compatibilities are [fix-prop-coherence] and [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii). Consequently the concrete operations form that datum. Its axioms are being verified from the named theorems, not assumed to prove the package. We may now apply the formal coherence statements in that datum. At finite coefficients the dualizing object and evaluation used here are exactly [def-trf-dualizing-complex]: its $a_X$ is separated finite type by step 1, and its constructible admissibility [def-trf-admissibility] is the adjunction, composition and conjugate-exchange datum just supplied in steps 3,5–8, together with the composition and exchange conjugates obtained by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] from those adjunctions (with the uniform preservation bounds supplied independently by [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum], as computed in step 20). In particular its displayed evaluation is the transpose of the identity of $D_XK$, so it is the evaluation used in the present biduality clause. This uses the dualizing-complex definition in the Künneth–Verdier unit, without invoking any of that unit’s three general product isomorphisms.

source.place: Clause (6): canonical biduality; verification of the formal datum

proof.text:
Apply [prop-sf-pf-coherence] to this verified datum. In particular its displayed base-change square identifies $Lg^*(\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L})$ with $\operatorname{PF}_{f',Lg'^*K,Lg^*L}$ through the two compact-support exchange maps and the monoidal pullback comparisons; this proves the base-change clause of (3). Its associativity pentagon, identity, compactification independence and coefficient comparisons give the remaining projection coherence. The ordinary and exceptional units and counits are coherent with composition, refinement and exchanges by [fix-prop-coherence]; more explicitly [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] sends the pasted compact-support comparisons to the pasted exceptional ones. Only conjugates between right adjoints of isomorphic left functors are automatically invertible: [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] gives $R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ and the pasted units/counits. We do not infer invertibility of an arbitrary square mate. At the finite stage the first projection input in (3) may be bounded constructible without finite Tor amplitude; the formal datum alone does not cover that larger domain. Here is the base-change check there, using the concrete formula of [def-exchange-projection]. Choose $f=pj$ and its base change $f'=p'j'$, and put $M=j_!K$. The proper projection map is the adjoint transpose of
$$Lp^*(Rp_*M\otimes^LL)\cong Lp^*Rp_*M\otimes^LLp^*L\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1}M\otimes^LLp^*L.$$
Transpose both paths around the proper projection/base-change square under $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$, using the ordinary adjunction of step 2 for $p,p'$. By the exchange formula in [def-exchange-projection], both transposes are the map
$$Lp'^*Lg^*(Rp_*M\otimes^LL)\cong L\bar g'^*Lp^*Rp_*M\otimes^LLp'^*Lg^*L\xrightarrow{L\bar g'^*\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1}L\bar g'^*M\otimes^LLp'^*Lg^*L.$$
For the path projecting before exchange, this follows by naturality of the counit and the triangle identity; for the path exchanging before projection, substitute the defining transpose of the exchange into the first tensor factor. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection equates the two paths. For the open factor use [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Both paths are maps between extensions by zero; their restrictions along $j'$ are the canonical tensor/pullback reassociation. The exact adjunction of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], with $j'^{-1}j'_!=\mathrm{id}$, identifies their Hom sets with the Hom sets of their restrictions, hence the paths agree. Pasting these proper and open squares gives the claimed compact-support projection/base-change square for every bounded constructible $K$ and finite-Tor $L$. Naturality is inherited from the displayed natural transformations; the remaining coherence on this larger domain is supplied by [fix-prop-projection-formula]. Thus no extra finite-Tor condition on $K$ has been imposed.

proof.text: For a finite-stage smooth $f$ of pure relative dimension $d$, [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] says precisely that $\gamma_{f,K}$ is invertible for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. Naturality and independence are [prop-pur-smooth-purity-naturality-cover]. Taking $K=\Lambda_Y$ yields $\omega_f\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$. At integral coefficients [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] supplies a morphism of normalized strict systems realizing these finite maps and gives its canonical reductions; [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] gives the scalar-transported isomorphisms. This is the lecture-notes diagonal/deformation route, as required by the finite smooth-purity theorem, rather than an assumption of orientation.

source.place: Clause (5): finite smooth purity and actual normalized coefficient passage

proof.text: Composition of the finite purity maps is the displayed equality of [thm-pur-composition-coherence]; finite arbitrary-base-change coherence is the commuting square of [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence], with the smooth pullback exchange defined by [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]. The counit after orientation is the normalized smooth trace, and [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] gives its transitivity and base-change compatibility. Transposing its base-change square under $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$ identifies the smooth pullback exchange with the transpose of $Lg^*\varepsilon_f\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$ written in (5). Integral and scalar coherences are [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] and [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence]; restricting their base-change assertion to étale $g$ gives exactly the higher-stage assertion required here.

source.place: Clause (5): composition and correctly typed smooth base-change/trace comparison

proof.text:
For the smooth exceptional product assertion at finite coefficients, put $M_i=Lf_i^*L_i(d_i)[2d_i]$, $H=L_1\boxtimes L_2$, and factor $f=f_1\times f_2$ as $a=f_1\times\mathrm{id}_{X_2}:X_1\times X_2\to Y_1\times X_2$ followed by $b=\mathrm{id}_{Y_1}\times f_2:Y_1\times X_2\to Y_1\times Y_2$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1),(2), these are smooth of dimensions $d_1,d_2$, and $ba$ is smooth of dimension $d_1+d_2$. The comparison to be checked is the map $M_1\boxtimes M_2\to Rf^!H$ obtained by canonical pullback/tensor reassociation followed by $\gamma_{f,H}$. Composition of the orientations in step 14 says that its adjoint transpose is the explicit chain
$$
R(ba)_!(M_1\boxtimes M_2)
\xrightarrow{\alpha_{b,a}^{-1}}Rb_!Ra_!\bigl(La^*(L_1\boxtimes M_2)(d_1)[2d_1]\bigr)
\xrightarrow{Rb_!\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{a,L_1\boxtimes M_2}}Rb_!(L_1\boxtimes M_2)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{b,H}}H.
$$
Here each trace is the oriented counit of [def-pur-smooth-trace]; the twist $d_2$ is already in $M_2$ when the first trace is applied. To compute this chain, base-change the $f_1$ trace along $Y_1\times X_2\to Y_1$ and extract the $M_2$ factor by the inverse projection formula. This gives $(\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f_1,L_1}\boxtimes1_{M_2})$ after the exchange and projection comparisons. Next base-change the $f_2$ trace along $Y_1\times Y_2\to Y_2$ and extract $L_1$ by the inverse projection formula, giving $(1_{L_1}\boxtimes\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f_2,L_2})$. These coefficient-factor formulas follow from the specified tensor map in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]: its transpose is inverse projection followed by the unit-coefficient counit, so tensoring an additional pulled-back factor inserts exactly another inverse projection; the associativity pentagon of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] identifies the two inverse projections. Base-change and transitivity of these traces are [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity]. The base-change square and pentagon of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] identify the preceding exchange/projection composite with the specified $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative]. Thus the displayed chain is
$$(\varepsilon_1\boxtimes\varepsilon_2)\circ\mathrm{Ku}_!\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{f_1,L_1}\boxtimes\gamma_{f_2,L_2}).$$
By [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](ii), this is the transpose of $\alpha\circ(\gamma_{f_1,L_1}\boxtimes\gamma_{f_2,L_2})$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves the required equality for every finite-Tor $L_i$, without invoking any of the general Künneth–Verdier isomorphisms.

source.place: Clause (5): expand the smooth step of sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier

proof.text:
For the Verdier exchange in (6), apply [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] with $N=\omega_Y$ and invert its displayed isomorphism. Follow it by $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(M,-)$ of the composition-conjugate isomorphism $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$; [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange] identifies the resulting canonical map and proves it natural and invertible on the stated finite-Tor domain. Here is the composition check explicitly. For a finite-Tor test object $T$ on $Z$, tensor–Hom and the ordinary and exceptional adjunctions identify
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(T,D_ZR(gf)_!M)
&=\operatorname{Hom}(R(gf)_!M\otimes^LT,\omega_Z)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(gf)_!(M\otimes^LL(gf)^*T),\omega_Z)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes^LL(gf)^*T,R(gf)^!\omega_Z)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L(gf)^*T,D_XM)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,R(gf)_*D_XM).
\end{aligned}
$$
The first isomorphism precomposes with $\operatorname{PF}_{gf,M,T}^{-1}$; the next is the exceptional Hom bijection, followed by the composition identification of the dualizing object. These are the tensor–Hom and adjunction maps defining the canonical exchange, using [sk-def-sf-operations](i). Computing first for $g$ and then for $f$ replaces that inverse projection by the two inverse projections for $g,f$, and the exceptional Hom bijection by its two successive bijections. The pentagon of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] equates those projection maps, while [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) equates the successive exceptional transposes with the composite transpose (the composite counit is $\varepsilon_g\circ Rg_!\varepsilon_f Rg^!$). The ordinary comparison [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] equates the final targets and the ordinary Hom bijections in their adjunction normalization. Thus for every $T$ the same Hom map is obtained. All endpoints are in the finite-Tor constructible categories by [thm-sf-ctf-stability], so Yoneda on those full categories gives precisely $Rg_*(\varepsilon_{f,M})\circ\varepsilon_{g,Rf_!M}$ after the stated comparisons. This proves composition at each coefficient stage on its specified domain.

source.place: Clause (6): canonical Verdier exchange and its composition equation

proof.text: If $X$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$ and $K$ is site-perfect, specialize [sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect] to $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It gives the natural isomorphism $D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ and identifies its biduality with coefficient biduality. For $X$ satisfying the additional smooth, geometrically connected and proper-or-finite-field-descent hypotheses, [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] gives the displayed global duality map as an isomorphism in the point category. Under the same hypotheses and with $K$ site-perfect, [sk-thm-sf-identification] identifies the transpose of the derived Poincaré pairing with its inverse, proving perfection. These additional hypotheses are kept; no integral degreewise perfect pairing is inferred from derived perfection.

source.place: Clause (6): smooth perfect comparison, global duality and derived pairing

proof.text: For (7), [thm-sf-ctf-stability](iv),(vii) puts $Rf_!K$ in the finite-Tor category so the second projection formula below is typed. Expand the map of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative]: first use $R(gq)_!\cong Rg_!Rq_!$, then inverse $\operatorname{PF}_{q,p^*K,L}$, inverse compact-support exchange $Rq_!p^*K\cong Lg^*Rf_!K$, symmetry, inverse $\operatorname{PF}_{g,L,Rf_!K}$, and symmetry once more. Each factor is invertible by the composition, exchange and projection statements already verified. [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] states precisely that composite and its naturality, symmetry, triple-product, base-change and projection specializations and both closed-subscheme compact-support forms. These are therefore the map and compatibilities required in (7); cohomology with supports via $Ri^!$ is a different object.

source.place: Clause (7): expand the relative product and retain its supported forms

proof.text: For (8), apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i)–(vii). It gives pullback, tensor, both direct images, general internal Hom, exceptional inverse image and duality on the stated finite-Tor domains, and coefficient passage to integral and field constructible categories. Its finite direct-image interval is $[a,b+2d]$ when $\dim X\le d$, its tensor interval is $[a+c,b+d']$, and its Hom interval is $[c-b-2d,d'-a+2d]$ when $\dim X\le d$, improving to $[c-b,d'-a]$ only for a site-perfect first argument. Integral intervals are uniform intervals of finite reductions; coefficient passage in (vii) gives their stated higher-stage interpretation. This proves the preservation part and these numerical cells, without identifying finite-Tor with site-perfect. For the finite étale internal-Hom preservation entry specifically, [det-rem-sf-matrix-hom-devissage] gives $R\cal Hom_A(K,L)\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$: the fixed algebraically closed field is separably closed and $A_{E,n}$ is finite $\ell$-primary. Thus the matrix’s finite-stage Hom entry agrees with the stability theorem just used; the numerical interval still comes from that theorem rather than from the matrix lemma.

source.place: Clause (8): preservation and direct-image/tensor/Hom interval cells

proof.text: For the exceptional intervals of (8), smooth purity from steps 13–14 changes $[a,b]$ to $[a-2d,b-2d]$. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with $\dim T\le d$, the open complement is Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and [thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional] supplies vanishing and constructibility with $c=2d$. Apply [prop-exc-closed-tor] first on the small étale site, where its $Ri^!$ is the right adjoint of the closed direct image, to obtain $[a,b+2d+1]$. To identify this with the package's functor, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a) allows the compactification $(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$, and [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] states that étale $i_*$ is exact. Hence the ordinary étale compact-support functor for this compactification is $Ri_*=i_*$, and [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identifies its ordinary étale exceptional adjoint with this $Ri^!$. For a pro-étale finite-Tor input $K$, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives a bounded constructible étale model $G$. By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii), $G$ has the same input Tor interval $[a,b]$. The transported-adjoint formula of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi) now identifies the package's value with $\nu_Z^*Ri^!G$, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i) carries its interval $[a,b+2d+1]$ back to the pro-étale site. Thus the closed-immersion interval is proved for the actual functor used in (8). For a general separated finite-type $f$, [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum] gives $[a-2D,b-2D+c]$ with $c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y)$ and $c=\max_U(c_U+1+2(D-d_U))$. Each term of this last maximum is $2D+2\dim Y+1$, so its interval is $[a-2D,b+2\dim Y+1]$. These constants are independent of the finite coefficient level. The coefficient reductions and adjunction comparisons of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] and the coefficient-passage clause [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii) give the uniform integral and field reading. Empty source has zero outputs; if the target is empty the source is empty too. Thus no empty maximum or negative-infinite scheme dimension enters an interval.
